messages.text: Hi there — I'm Sarah, an AI researcher with HeliumDeploy. Thank you so much for taking 25 minutes to do this — it really means a lot. Honestly, the more you can share with me, the better — we're aiming for about fifteen hundred words of feedback together, so please don't worry about going long. The founders read every word of these chats, so what you say actually shapes what HD does next. As a thank-you you'll get a $75 discount code at the end. I think on Reddit,

Yeah.

Uh, I don't think so.

Not really. I'm waiting to for the prices to drop.
Got it — waiting for the price to drop. How long are you willing to wait? Like, are you checking weekly, or is this a "maybe end of year" thing?
Yeah. I'm a check checkmate. Almost daily, but I can wait a few months.
Daily checks but can wait months — that's a real watch-list behavior. What price would actually make you click "buy"? Like what's the number where you stop waiting?

$450-$600 max — got it. So roughly $100-$250 off current. Let me push back a bit: at $699 for a BM1373-based miner, that's actually competitive on $/TH for new-gen silicon. What's the real blocker — the absolute dollar amount, or something else like electricity cost, or are you saving up?
The price.

Just the absolute price — fair. So $699 is just too much to put down right now, regardless of the $/TH math. Is that because you're treating mining as a hobby budget — like, "I'll spend $X on this and no more"? Or is it more that you want to see if the chip drops further before committing?
Because I know the chances of hitting a byte Bitcoin block is very low, so I don't want to invest very much money into it.

There it is — you're treating it like a lottery ticket, and you're not going to over-spend on a lottery ticket. That makes total sense. So the Gamma at AliExpress prices fits that math, but $699 doesn't.

So let me ask — if it IS basically a lottery ticket, why do it at all? What do you get out of running the Gamma every day?
Nothing regarding the chance to getting the block.
Right, so the block-hit isn't really the point. Then what IS the point for you? What do you actually enjoy about having the Gamma running?
Uh, participating in the Bitcoin network. And, uh, having a chance

Supporting the network plus the lottery chance — got it. Tell me more about "participating in the network" — why does that matter to you personally? Is it ideological, like you believe in decentralization, or something else?
Yeah. I believe in it. I have, uh, some Bitcoin. And I like it.

And something like, uh, hobby and to love. No. I'm more about Bitcoin. Network.
Got it — hobby plus learning more about how the network actually works. So when you set up the Gamma — did you tinker with it? Like flash AxeOS, overclock, mess with voltage, any of that?

Google. And previous, uh, experience with the PC overclocking.

Ah, PC overclocking background — that explains the comfort with voltage and thermals. So you came in already knowing the muscle memory.

Done with the Gamma — okay. So the next move is a second miner, not tweaking the first one further. And that second miner is the Nexus S1 once it drops to your price.

Because I like the open source, not some vendor specific uh, format.

No. It's only my preference.

WiFi's fine for the Gamma. What about when you add a second miner — does the math change with two units on WiFi, or still fine?
Yeah. Maybe. For, uh, something we'd because they were harsh, I would prefer the violence.

Got it — for higher-hashrate units like the Nexus S1, you'd want wired. Makes sense — more at stake per disconnect.

Let me show you one more thing — a hypothetical feature inside the HD customer dashboard. A "Top Miners" leaderboard — opt-in, ranks customers by hashrate, you'd see where you stand. Would you actually use this, or feel cringe?
Not really.
Not really — why? Privacy thing, or just don't care about the ranking?
I don't care about ranking because, uh, always will be somebody with higher cash rate than me.

Fair — you're never going to top a leaderboard against someone running a farm, so what's the point. That's a real answer.

So you've told me a lot — let me reflect back what I'm hearing: you're a tinkerer, came in via Reddit chasing the BM1373, treating mining as a network-participation hobby with a lottery upside, very price-disciplined ($600 ceiling), open-source matters for trust reasons, and the Gamma is dialed in at 1.6 TH/28W in your bedroom with Noctuas.

One thing I want to circle back on — you mentioned AliExpress for the Gamma. Any concerns buying from there? DOA risk, support, anything?
No. I had a good experience with early express so far.
Good — no friction there. So honestly for you, HD would need to beat AliExpress on either price or product (like exclusive BM1373 stuff) to win the next purchase. Is that fair?
Hello?
